transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main reason is I keep getting pulled off track by tiny stuff. Like over the past year or so, I’ll be in my office trying to focus on something important, and my phone buzzes, or someone walks by the door, and suddenly I’m not doing the thing anymore.

Even sometimes it’s not even something happening—just some random thought, like about my in-laws or something completely unrelated, and I’m off on that before I even realize it. It’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
When you were a child, did you also have a hard time staying focused?

Yeah, I mean… looking back, yeah, I think so. School was kind of a mess for me in that way. Teachers were always moving my seat around—not even just once—because I’d be talking too much, or I’d get up without asking.

And I remember blurting out answers before they even finished the question, which… I don’t know, at the time it just felt like I was excited or knew the answer. But yeah, that was around when I was a kid too.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about different parts of your life, even when there isn’t an immediate reason to?

I don’t know… I mean, I worry about stuff like anyone does, I guess. Work things, family things. But “a lot” is hard to say.

Sometimes I’ll get stuck on something random, like whether I forgot to send an email, and then that reminds me of three other things, and then I’m thinking about the garage or some bill or—sorry, that’s probably not what you mean. I’m not sure I’d say I’m just worrying for no reason all the time.
Have these focus problems caused significant problems for you at work?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still keeping up overall. It’s not like everything’s falling apart, and I don’t want to make it sound dramatic.

But it does cause problems. Like in meetings, I’ll miss pieces or the conversation goes sideways because I jump in too fast, and then people get frustrated. Or when I’m mentoring someone, I’ll mean to stay with what they’re saying, but I end up pulling it into some other story or idea, and I can tell they’re kind of waiting for me to come back around.

And at home too—sorry, I know you asked about work—but it affects plans with my family, and my wife gets annoyed because it feels like I’m not reliable in the moment. So yeah, I’m managing, but I think people are losing patience with it a bit.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?

Um… I don’t think so. Not most of the day, at least. I mean, I get frustrated or kind of worn out sometimes, especially when a day feels like it’s gotten away from me, but I wouldn’t call it depressed.

Like, I can have a bad morning and then something at work pulls me in, or I’m dealing with some random thing at home—actually yesterday I spent way too long trying to find this one receipt, which is stupid because it wasn’t even that important—but anyway, no, I haven’t really noticed feeling down most of the day for the past couple weeks.
Do you spend much of the day feeling worried or on edge?

I’m not sure I’d say much of the day, no. Like, I get wound up sometimes if there are a bunch of things happening at once, or if I think I forgot something—but then I’ll get distracted by something else and I’m onto that.

“On edge” is hard to pin down, because sometimes I’m just moving fast, if that makes sense. Not necessarily worried, just… keyed up. But I haven’t really noticed sitting around worried all day or anything like that.
Did these problems start after a specific stressful event or major life change?

Kind of, yeah. I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it one big event exactly, but it’s been noticeably harder to manage for… about a year and a couple months, I think.

That’s around when the conflict with my in-laws started taking over more of our family life. There were all these conversations and plans and tension—sorry, that’s a whole other story—but yeah, that’s when it started feeling harder to keep a handle on things.
When the conflict with your in-laws settles down, do your focus problems noticeably improve?

Not really in a clean way, no. I mean, when things are calmer with them I’m less caught up in that whole… family drama loop, but my focus still gets knocked off really easily.

That’s actually kind of why I came in. For the past year or so, it’s like the smallest thing will pull me away before I can stop it—a phone buzz, someone walking past my office, or even just a random thought about my in-laws. And then I’m off track, and sometimes I don’t even realize I’ve switched gears until I’m already doing something else.
As a child, did these attention and impulsivity problems happen at home too, or mainly just at school?

Yeah, looking back, it was there when I was a kid too. I remember at school, teachers were always moving my seat because I’d talk too much or get up without asking.

I’d also blurt stuff out before they were even done asking the question—like I thought I knew where they were going with it. At home… I’m trying to remember. School is what stands out more because you’d get in trouble for it there, you know? But it definitely wasn’t something that just started recently.
As a child, did you also get distracted or act impulsively at home?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, home is harder for me to remember clearly because school was where it got pointed out all the time. Teachers were always moving my seat because I talked too much, or I’d get up without asking, or I’d blurt out an answer before they even finished asking.

At home it probably showed up too, just… nobody was keeping a behavior chart on the fridge or anything. Well, actually my mom did try stuff like that for chores, but that’s not really what you asked. But yeah, looking back, this wasn’t only recent. It was around when I was a kid too.
